b: Friends, let me introduce you to my all-time favorite pie, the incomparable Sweet Potato Pie! Ok, I realize that’s a big statement, but it’s true. This creamy sweet potato pie recipe is made with baked sweet potatoes for a deep, caramelized flavor, warm spices, and a flaky, buttery crust. It comes in at under a dollar per serving and it can be made in advance to free up your oven on Thanksgiving day. This easy, beginner-friendly pie is definitely a classic Thanksgiving dessert that will steal the show at this year’s holiday dinner!

“I made this for the first time for Thanksgiving and it was a huge hit. Sooooo good!!! Thank you for sharing your recipe. I didn’t get a chance to take a photo but it was as beautiful as it was delicious. No cracks!!”

Growing up in the South, there was always a fun, lighthearted debate over which pie was better: sweet potato pie or pumpkin pie. Every family seems to have its own version of this classic Southern dessert, from the spices they use to how they prepare the sweet potatoes. For my version, I bake the sweet potatoes instead of boiling them or using canned. Baking brings out their natural sweetness and gives the filling a richer, more caramelized flavor (that you don’t get from boiling alone!). Then I blend them with butter, brown and white sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, eggs, and evaporated milk to make a smooth, buttery, lightly spiced filling that really lets the sweet potatoes shine.

So if you love our pumpkin pie, I think you’ll love this one, too! Sweet potato pie has a slightly denser, creamier texture, and the baked sweet potatoes give it a deeper flavor that doesn’t rely entirely on the spices. I wanted to make this recipe as easy as possible, and since so much of the flavor comes from the filling, I skipped making the pastry from scratch. Instead, I use an inexpensive store-bought crust to keep this homemade Thanksgiving dessert simple. As for which pie is better? I’m not choosing sides. They’re both equally delicious! 😉

Measure the sweet potatoes after cooking. I use 2 lbs of whole sweet potatoes because that reliably gives me the 2 cups of cooked, mashed sweet potato I need for this pie. Measure out exactly 2 cups after cooking, rather than using everything you’ve baked. Adding extra sweet potato can leave you with too much filling for your crust.

Use a 9-inch deep-dish pie crust. There’s a generous amount of custard filling in this recipe, so a regular shallow pie crust will overflow. I use a store-bought deep-dish crust in a disposable aluminum pan (see below for more help on choosing the right pie crust). Making two pies? Double all the ingredients and divide the filling between two deep-dish crusts. Check each pie for doneness, especially if you’re baking them together.

Bake the sweet potatoes until they’re super soft. I always recommend baking rather than boiling for this pie. Boiled potatoes can absorb extra water, which may thin the filling and make it watery, while baking concentrates their natural sweetness. A knife or fork should slide easily through the center. It’s better to have slightly overcooked sweet potatoes than undercooked ones here.

Blend until smooth. I recommend mixing the pie filling with a hand mixer until extremely smooth OR using a food processor. If you’re noticing a lot of “strings” in your mashed sweet potatoes, you can remove them carefully with a fork, or press the mashed sweet potatoes through a fine mesh strainer to ensure your pie filling comes out extra velvety smooth!
Let the potatoes and melted butter cool slightly. Both should be cool or just barely warm before adding the eggs. If they’re too hot, the eggs may start cooking before the pie goes into the oven.

Look for a gentle jiggle in the center. After 50-55 minutes, the edges should look set and slightly puffed, while the center can still wobble a little when you gently shake the pan. It shouldn’t look liquid. The custard continues firming as it cools, so allow 2-3 hours for it to fully set before slicing. Cool at room temperature for no more than 2 hours, then refrigerate to finish setting if needed.

I use a 9-inch deep-dish pie crust for this recipe. I like the premade ones that come in disposable aluminum pans because they’re affordable and save me from making pastry from scratch. They usually come in packs of two, so you can keep one frozen for another day or double the recipe to make two pies!

Make sure the package specifically says ‘deep dish’ (like the two options shown on the right in my photo below). A regular 9-inch crust (like the Great Value 9″ Pie Crusts on the left) is shallower, so you’ll have leftover filling. You might be able to divide the filling between two shallower crusts, but I haven’t tested that or the baking time. I recommend saving those for another recipe, like our pecan pie, instead.
Look for pie crusts labeled ‘deep dish’ (like the two on the right here) and save the shallower pie crusts (as shown on the left) for other pie recipes.
Do I Need to Blind-Bake the Pie Crust?

It’s optional, but I recommend it! Blind-baking simply means baking the empty crust before adding the filling. It helps give the crust a crisp, lightly golden bottom rather than a soggy one. I also use a foil pie shield during the final bake to prevent the edges from getting too dark.
How to Serve Sweet Potato Pie

This easy pie makes 8 standard-sized slices, but you can cut them smaller or larger depending on how many people you’re serving. Be sure to let the pie set completely before slicing, or the custard filling may be too soft to hold its shape. For those lovely, neat slices, I use a sharp knife and wipe the blade clean between each cut. A dollop of homemade whipped cream is a classic topping, and its light, airy texture is so delicious with the buttery sweet potato filling. But if you’ve got a real sweet tooth, try a drizzle of our easy caramel sauce for an extra buttery, caramel-sweet dessert!

Impress your guests with this creamy & delicious Sweet Potato Pie recipe! It adds the perfect touch to finish your Thanksgiving meal.
Cook Time 2 hours hours 20 minutes minutes
Total Time 3 hours hours 40 minutes minutes
Gather ingredients and preheat the oven to 400°F.

Wash and dry the sweet potatoes, then prick them several times with a fork. Place the sweet potatoes on a parchment lined baking sheet and bake for 50-60 minutes or until tender and you can easily slide a knife or fork in the center. It’s better to have them a bit overcooked (super soft) than undercooked for this recipe! Set the baked sweet potatoes aside to cool.
Lower oven temperature to 350°F. Next blind-bake the pie crust. Prick the bottom and sides of the crust a few times with a fork.
Add a piece of parchment paper inside the center of the crust and place pie weights (or dry beans) on top.

Bake the crust in the oven for 15 minutes. After 15 minutes, remove the pie weights and parchment and return the crust to the oven to bake for another 10 minutes. Remove crust from the oven and let cool. Around this time, you'll also need to melt the butter for the filling, then it needs a little time to cool.
Now make the pie filling. Scoop about 2 cups of the sweet potato flesh from the baked sweet potatoes and add to a large bowl (save any leftovers for another recipe!)
Using a hand mixer, mash or blend the sweet potato flesh until very smooth.

Add the cooled but still melted butter, brown sugar, white sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, nutmeg, a pinch of salt, the eggs, and evaporated milk to the bowl. Blend the ingredients together with a hand mixer until smooth. Make sure the sweet potato and the butter are cool/just barely warm so they don’t cook the eggs! Mix until completely uniform and mostly smooth.

Pour the sweet potato pie filling into the crust. Add a foil ring around the edges to prevent the crust from over-browning. Bake the pie in the preheated 350°F oven for 50-55 minutes or until the pie is mostly set and the center is no longer liquid. It’s ok if the center has a slight jiggle when you shake the pan.

Remove the pie from the oven. It will be slightly domed and puffed around the edges. Let the pie cool at room temperature for at least 2 hours (move to the fridge after 2 hours if it needs longer to set). Serve at room temperature or cover and refrigerate to serve later.

*Baking your sweet potatoes in the oven gives them a deeper flavor. I buy about 2 lbs. (roughly 2-3 sweet potatoes, depending on size). Cooked with the flesh scooped out, this yields around 450-500 grams (about 16-18 oz). For this recipe, you need 2 cups of cooked sweet potato flesh, so plan to buy at least 2 lbs of sweet potatoes to make sure you don’t fall short. If you have extra, save it for another recipe! Our sweet potato biscuits are a delicious option and use 1 cup of mashed sweet potato.

**Make sure your melted salted butter has cooled until it’s just barely warm before mixing it into the filling so it doesn’t start cooking the eggs. If you’re using unsalted butter, increase the pinch of salt in the recipe to ½ tsp.

***I like using two types of sugar because brown sugar adds a deeper, caramel sweetness, and white sugar sweetens the filling without adding more molasses flavor. You can use all white sugar in a pinch, but I prefer the richer flavor you get from the combination.

****You only need ⅓ cup, not the whole can of evaporated milk. Evaporated milk is concentrated, unsweetened milk that gives the custard a creamy texture without adding too much extra liquid. Don’t confuse it with sweetened condensed milk, which contains added sugar and isn’t a direct substitute. You can save the remaining evaporated milk for mashed potatoes, soups, or coffee.

I use a store-bought 9-inch deep-dish pie crust. Always check the package directions, as brands can vary. The frozen crust I use says to let it thaw for about 15 minutes before pricking it with a fork (this helps prevent cracking). Leave it in its disposable aluminum pan. You can also make our 3-ingredient pie crust from scratch. If you’re making your crust from scratch, I recommend pre-baking it, too, following the blind-baking instructions in the recipe. Don’t forget to protect the edges with a foil pie shield during the final bake!

To get a head start on making this pie, you can bake your sweet potatoes a day or two in advance. Then once the sweet potatoes are completely cool, just wrap them tightly with foil or store them in an airtight container in the fridge. They’ll be already cooked and ready to go the next day!
OR you can make the entire pie a day or two in advance. Let the pie completely cool at room temperature (for about an hour or two), then cover the pie with plastic wrap or place it in an airtight container and store in the fridge.

Fridge: Store leftover pie tightly covered in plastic wrap or in an airtight container in the fridge for 3-4 days after baking. I like wrapping the whole pie and slipping it into a large storage bag, but individual slices can be stored separately. Since this is an egg-and-milk custard, refrigerate it within 2 hours of baking.

Freezer: Custard pies don’t always freeze well, as the filling can become slightly grainy or watery and the crust may soften after thawing. If you want to freeze leftovers, wrap individual chilled slices tightly in plastic wrap, followed by foil, and place them in a freezer-safe bag or container. Freeze for up to 2 months for the best quality, then thaw overnight in the refrigerator before serving.

How to Make Sweet Potato Pie Step-by-Step Photos

Gather all your ingredients: Preheat the oven to 400°F. If you’re using a frozen store-bought pie crust, plan to take it out of the freezer about 15 minutes before you’re ready to blind-bake it. This gives it time to thaw slightly so it doesn’t crack when you prick it with a fork.
(I’m also showing the whole can of evaporated milk in my ingredient photo so you know what to look for at the store, but you’ll only need ⅓ cup for this recipe!)
Bake the sweet potatoes: Wash and dry 2 lbs. of sweet potatoes (about 2-3, depending on size), then prick them several times with a fork.

Place them on a parchment-lined baking sheet and bake for 50-60 minutes, or until a knife or fork slides easily into the center. I prefer them a little overcooked rather than undercooked for this pie. The softer they are, the easier they’ll be to blend into a smooth filling. Set aside to cool.

Prepare the pie crust: Lower the oven temperature to 350°F. Prick the bottom and sides of 1 deep-dish pie crust a few times with a fork. This helps release steam and prevents the pastry from puffing up too much as it blind-bakes.

Blind-bake the crust: Line the crust with parchment paper and add pie weights or dried beans (I’m using dried chickpeas here) to help keep the pastry in place. Bake for 15 minutes, then carefully remove the parchment and weights and bake for another 10 minutes. Remove the crust from the oven and let it cool.
Now’s also a good time to melt your 6 Tbsp of salted butter so it can cool slightly before you make the filling.

I also highly recommend creating a crust shield so the crust of your pie stays perfectly golden during the second bake! Do this by folding a large piece of tinfoil into a square, placing the folded angle towards the center of the pie.

When it’s about in the center, trim it at an angle. Discard the circle you cut out of the middle, and use what’s left to shield your crust from getting burnt by gently placing it over the pie once it’s filled. For now, set it aside.

Measure the sweet potato: Once the sweet potatoes are cool enough to handle, scoop out exactly 2 cups of cooked sweet potato flesh and add it to a large bowl. You might have a little left over, depending on the size of your potatoes. Don’t add the extra to the filling.

Mash until smooth: Use a hand mixer to blend the sweet potato flesh until it’s very smooth. A potato masher works, too, but I find a hand mixer (or food processor) gives the creamiest result. If you notice any stringy fibers, fish them out with a fork or press the mashed sweet potatoes through a fine-mesh strainer for a silkier filling.

Make the sweet potato pie filling: Add the 6 Tbsp of melted and cooled salted butter, ½ cup brown sugar, ⅓ cup granulated sugar, 1 tsp vanilla extract, ½ tsp cinnamon, ¼ tsp nutmeg, a pinch of salt, 2 large eggs, and ⅓ cup evaporated milk to the mashed sweet potatoes. Blend everything together with a hand mixer until completely smooth and uniform. Make sure the sweet potatoes and melted butter are cool or just barely warm before adding the eggs.

Fill the pie crust: Pour the sweet potato filling into your prepared 9-inch deep-dish pie crust. The filling should fit comfortably if you’ve measured out the 2 cups of cooked sweet potato flesh and are using the correct crust size.

Protect the crust and bake: Place the aluminum foil pie shield loosely around the edges of the filled pie. Since we’ve already blind-baked the crust, this helps keep the exposed edges from getting too dark while the custard finishes cooking. Bake at 350°F for 50-55 minutes, or until the filling is mostly set and the center is no longer liquid. A slight jiggle in the middle is perfectly fine.

Let the pie cool and set: Remove the pie from the oven. Don’t worry if it looks slightly domed or puffed around the edges. It’ll settle back down as it cools. Let the pie cool at room temperature for 2 hours before slicing. If the filling needs more time to firm up, transfer it to the refrigerator to finish setting. Serve at room temperature or chilled from the fridge. Enjoy.
